chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) and ‘Ali ibn al-Ḥusayn narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Mūsā ibn al-Faḍl, from Ḥanān, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him): ‘What do you say about the Ziyārah of the grave of Abī ‘Abdillāh al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him)? For it has reached us from some of them that it equals one Ḥajj and one ‘Umrah.’ He replied: ‘Do not be surprised [by what is achieved] by all of this statement, but go to his Ziyārah and do not abandon him, for verily he is the Master of the Martyrs and the Master of the Youth of Paradise, and he is similar to Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā (peace be upon him), and over the two of them the heavens and the earth wept.’

My father and Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn al-Walīd narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār, from ‘Abd al-Ṣamad ibn Muḥammad, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), the same as it.

My father (may Allah the Exalted have mercy on him) and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā‘īl ibn Bazī‘, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), the same as it.

key_terms.زِيَارَة: Ziyarah (visitation, especially of graves or shrines)
key_terms.يَحْيَى بْنُ زَكَرِيَّا: Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā (John son of Zechariah)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting the grave of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) validates the tradition that visiting the grave of Imām al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) equals one Ḥajj and one ‘Umrah, emphasizing the necessity of consistent visitation (ziyarah) rather than neglect. He elevates al-Ḥusayn’s status as the Master of Martyrs and Youth of Paradise, drawing a profound theological parallel to Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā, noting that the heavens and earth wept over both, thereby linking cosmic grief to spiritual merit. This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* underscores the Shi‘i emphasis on the intercessory and redemptive power of the Ahl al-Bayt’s graves.
